bug_description.normalized: GnuTLS first consumes the attacker-controlled 13-byte DER blob in `gnutls_pkcs12_import` by aliasing `data->data` and `data->size` into local `_data`, then decodes `_data` into the internal PKCS#12 ASN.1 tree. During the first bag extraction in `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse`, `gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag` calls `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`, which allocates `char oid[MAX_OID_SIZE]` on the stack without initialization. `asn1_read_value` then decodes the PoC's `authSafe.contentType` OID bytes `06 01 20` into the short textual OID `0.32` at the front of `oid`, leaving the rest of the stack buffer indeterminate. The code immediately executes `strcmp(oid, DATA_OID)`, where `DATA_OID` is the 20-character literal `"1.2.840.113549.1.7.1"`. The optimized compare touches a 21-byte region including the trailing NUL, so it reads past the initialized `0.32\0` prefix into `oid`'s uninitialized tail. MemorySanitizer reports the first poisoned byte at offset 5 and attributes the uninitialized value to `oid`'s stack allocation in `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the fuzz buffer: `gnutls_pkcs12_import` copies the incoming datum pointer and size into local `_data`, creating the raw-byte alias used by the DER decoder in the next step.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness constructs `gnutls_datum_t raw`, assigns `raw.data = (unsigned char *)data; raw.size = size;`, and passes `&raw` to `gnutls_pkcs12_import` (fuzz/gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer.c:29,38-45). The staged PoC is the exact 13-byte blob `30 0b 02 00 30 07 06 01 20 a0 01 20 ff`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the uninitialized tail of stack buffer `oid`. Step 4 allocates the full buffer without initialization, and step 5 overwrites only the short textual OID prefix before `strcmp` reads past it.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `strcmp` compares `oid` against the fixed literal `DATA_OID` (`1.2.840.113549.1.7.1`). In the witnessed run the compare is lowered to a 21-byte read, so it consumes `oid[5]` and later bytes from the uninitialized tail beyond the initialized `0.32\0` prefix.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 5 inside [..., 21)` and points back to the stack allocation of `oid` in `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`.

root_cause.description: The stack buffer `oid` is declared without initialization even though later logic compares it against the fixed 20-character `DATA_OID` literal with `strcmp` after only a short textual OID has been written into the front of the buffer.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed contentType `0.32`, only `oid[0..4]` become `0.32\0`; `oid[5..]` remain indeterminate. A correct fix would zero-initialize `oid` before the read or avoid a fixed-literal string compare that touches beyond the initialized prefix.

parser_admitted.condition: `result == ASN1_SUCCESS` for the 13-byte witness, so `gnutls_pkcs12_import` accepts the DER blob and stores the parsed tree in `pkcs12->pkcs12` for later bag extraction.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the 13-byte PoC as `gnutls_datum_t raw`, imports it with `gnutls_pkcs12_import`, and later reaches the first `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` bag extraction.

The vulnerable import path first aliases the raw buffer into local `_data`, then decodes `_data` into the internal ASN.1 object `pkcs12->pkcs12`; the malformed top-level `authSafe.contentType` survives this import.
The first bag extraction reuses the imported PKCS#12 tree and calls `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` on the top-level `authSafe` object.

The helper allocates stack buffer `oid` without initialization, writes only the short textual contentType OID prefix into it, and then `strcmp` reads the uninitialized tail while comparing against `DATA_OID`.

fine_trace.note: Copies the attacker-controlled datum pointer and size into local `_data`. Because the harness passes `GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER`, the PEM-decoding block is skipped and `_data` remains a direct alias of the raw fuzz bytes.

Consumes the raw bytes aliased in step 1 and materializes them as the internal ASN.1 tree `pkcs12->pkcs12`. For the staged witness this returns `ASN1_SUCCESS`, preserving the malformed top-level `authSafe.contentType` for later reads.

On the first bag iteration driven by `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse`, `gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag` passes the imported PKCS#12 tree into `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`, so that helper reads the attacker-controlled top-level `authSafe` fields.
Allocates stack buffer `oid` without initialization. MSAN later attributes the poisoned bytes consumed at the sink to this stack allocation.

Reads the attacker-controlled `authSafe.contentType` OID from the imported ASN.1 tree into `oid`. For witness bytes `06 01 20`, the front of the buffer becomes textual OID `0.32\0`; the remaining bytes in `oid` stay as the uninitialized stack contents from step 4.

This is the only guard before the compare. For the staged witness `asn1_read_value` succeeds, so the error-return path is skipped and execution continues with partially initialized `oid`; there is no separate check that the rest of `oid` was cleared or that comparison is limited to the bytes actually written.

MSAN sink. `strcmp` compares `oid` against `DATA_OID\0` (`1.2.840.113549.1.7.1`), and the optimized compare touches a 21-byte region. `oid[0..4]` hold `0.32\0`, but `oid[5]` and later still come from the uninitialized tail created at step 4, so MemorySanitizer reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 5 inside [..., 21)`.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `oid` in the stack frame of `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`; the declaration itself is at line 53.

format.name: DER-encoded PKCS#12 blob consumed by `gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer` via `gnutls_pkcs12_import`
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact 13-byte DER blob `30 0b 02 00 30 07 06 01 20 a0 01 20 ff`. It imports as a PKCS#12 structure whose top-level `authSafe.contentType` is the short OID `0.32` (DER `06 01 20`). During the first `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` bag extraction, `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` reads that textual OID into stack buffer `oid` and immediately compares it against the 21-byte literal `DATA_OID\0`. Only the `0.32\0` prefix is initialized; `oid[5]` and later bytes remain poisoned, and the compare triggers MSAN at offset 5. This contract is limited to the staged witness layout and observed path, not all malformed PKCS#12 inputs or all short OIDs.
